title: Transfers without deadlock
description:
A bank has several accounts, each with its own mutex so that unrelated transfers do not wait for each other. A transfer must lock **two** accounts. If one thread locks A then B while another locks B then A, each can end up holding one lock and waiting for ever for the other: a **deadlock**.

Write `class Bank`:

- `Bank(std::size_t accounts, long long startingBalance)`
- `bool transfer(std::size_t from, std::size_t to, long long amount)`: moves the money and returns `true`. Returns `false`, changing nothing, if `from == to`, the amount is not positive, or `from` has too little.
- `long long balance(std::size_t account) const`
- `long long total() const`: the sum of all balances.

`std::scoped_lock lock{ mutexA, mutexB };` locks both mutexes together using an algorithm that cannot deadlock. The tests run threads transferring in opposite directions and check that the total never changes.

`std::mutex` cannot be copied or moved, so a `std::vector<Account>` of structs containing one must be built at its final size and never resized.
hints: Check the rules (`from != to`, positive amount) before locking anything.

`std::scoped_lock lock{ m_mutex[from], m_mutex[to] };` locks both at once without the deadlock; then check the balance and move the money. Keep the mutexes in a `std::vector<std::mutex>` (or `std::unique_ptr<std::mutex[]>`), sized in the constructor.
